description: We are second-year B.Tech AI & ML students interested in space exploration and healthcare innovation. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we developed COSMOCURA, an astronaut health intelligence system that organizes crew health information, supports wellness monitoring, and provides structured guidance. Our interests include software development, research, and problem-solving. We value teamwork, curiosity, clear communication, and learning through real-world challenges.
summary:
COSMOCURA is an Astronaut Health Intelligence System developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. During long-duration space missions, astronauts face unique health challenges, including communication delays, isolation, altered gravity, radiation exposure and limited access to immediate medical support.

COSMOCURA addresses these challenges through a unified, local-first digital health-support workspace. It brings together crew health monitoring, guided measurements, interactive body exploration, wellness tracking, medical records, emergency guidance and locally generated medical handoff summaries.

Built using React, Python FastAPI and SQLite, the prototype enables crew members to organize and review health-related information through a single interface, without depending on cloud connectivity during local operation.

Our vision is to explore how accessible, organized and mission-oriented digital health-support technology can contribute to astronaut health awareness and future human space exploration.
details:
COSMOCURA — ASTRONAUT HEALTH INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM

1. THE PROBLEM: HEALTHCARE BEYOND EARTH

Human space exploration presents healthcare challenges that extend beyond the capabilities of conventional healthcare environments. During long-duration missions, astronauts may experience radiation exposure, altered gravity, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, and hostile or closed environments.

Communication delays, limited medical resources and the absence of immediate access to healthcare professionals make the organization and accessibility of crew health information particularly important.

The challenge is not simply recording health information. It is ensuring that relevant information can be organized, reviewed and communicated when traditional healthcare support may be difficult to access.

2. OUR SOLUTION: COSMOCURA

COSMOCURA is an Astronaut Health Intelligence System developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project explores a local-first digital health-support workspace that brings multiple astronaut health-related capabilities together in one unified, mission-oriented application.

Instead of separating health measurements, wellness information, medical records and emergency guidance across different tools, COSMOCURA provides a centralized environment for crew members to organize and review their health-related information.

The central idea is to make essential health information more accessible and understandable, particularly in environments where continuous communication with Earth cannot be assumed.

3. CORE SYSTEM CAPABILITIES

The current working prototype includes:

• Mission Overview: A centralized dashboard presenting crew information and health-related indicators.

• Crew Management: Create, update and manage individual crew profiles.

• Crew Health Monitoring: Record and review manually entered health measurements.

• Guided Measurements: A structured interface that supports the recording of health measurements.

• Interactive Body Explorer: An interactive way to explore body-related health information.

• Emergency Center: Categorized emergency information and structured guidance with appropriate safety disclaimers.

• Medical Records: Create, organize and review crew medical records.

• Crew Wellness: Record sleep, mood, stress, fatigue and wellness notes.

• Wellness History: Review previously recorded wellness information.

• Spaceflight Hazard Awareness: Explore the five major human spaceflight hazards identified by NASA: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and hostile or closed environments.

• Mission Environment Profiles: Explore mission-related environmental considerations.

• Medical Handoff Brief: Generate and copy a locally prepared summary of crew health information to support information continuity.

These capabilities are designed to work together as parts of a single health-information workspace rather than as isolated functions.

4. TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE AND IMPLEMENTATION

COSMOCURA follows a local-first software architecture.

The frontend is developed using React and JavaScript, providing the interface through which users interact with the application.

The backend is developed using Python and FastAPI. It processes application requests and manages information through a local SQLite database, with SQLAlchemy handling database integration and Pydantic supporting data validation.

The local architecture allows the prototype to manage application records without requiring a cloud-hosted database or continuous external connectivity. The backend service must remain running during application use.

The Medical Handoff Brief organizes available health information into a readable report that can be copied locally. It is not automatically transmitted to spacecraft or mission control.

Technology stack:

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite.

Backend: Python, FastAPI.

Database: SQLite.

Database integration: SQLAlchemy.

Data validation: Pydantic.

Interface icons: Lucide React.

Development environment: Visual Studio Code.

Version control and source hosting: Git and GitHub.

5. IMPLEMENTATION AND FUNCTIONAL TESTING

COSMOCURA was developed as a functional software prototype, with its principal application workflows manually tested.

Testing demonstrated:

• Crew profile creation, editing and deletion.

• Recording health measurements and viewing them within Crew Health.

• Navigation through emergency information and safety guidance.

• Recording wellness check-ins and reviewing wellness history.

• Creating medical records and confirming that records remain available after a browser refresh.

• Generating a Medical Handoff Brief and copying its text.

• Responsive interface behaviour on smaller screens.

These demonstrations provide evidence of the prototype's implemented functionality. They do not represent clinical validation, medical accuracy testing or operational testing in spaceflight.

6. RELEVANCE TO NASA'S CHALLENGE AND USE OF NASA RESOURCES

COSMOCURA directly addresses astronaut health-information management in the context of human space exploration.

NASA Human Research Program resources concerning the five hazards of human spaceflight, human spaceflight risks and ongoing astronaut health research informed our understanding of the problem and the design of the project's hazard-awareness capabilities.

Canadian Space Agency publications concerning astronaut radiation monitoring and space-based research provided additional context.

These resources are used as research and design references. The current prototype does not download or process live NASA datasets, connect to NASA systems or integrate spacecraft radiation-monitoring instruments.

Our approach is to build a software foundation around astronaut health-information organization while identifying how validated space-agency data and mission-approved systems could be incorporated in future development.

7. INNOVATION AND CREATIVITY

The main innovation explored by COSMOCURA is the integration of multiple health-support workflows into one local-first application designed around the conditions of human spaceflight.

Its approach combines health monitoring, wellness tracking, medical records, emergency information and medical handoff reporting within a single interface.

The project also explores an important design consideration for future missions: essential health-related information should not depend entirely on continuous cloud connectivity.

By considering both the information needs of astronauts and the limitations of communication in deep-space environments, COSMOCURA presents an integrated approach to astronaut health-support software.

8. IMPACT, ACCESSIBILITY AND FUTURE POTENTIAL

COSMOCURA aims to support more organized health-information management and improve access to relevant crew health information.

Its intended impact is to explore how digital systems can help crew members maintain awareness of health-related information and support information continuity when communication with Earth may be delayed.

The project was developed using widely available development tools and open-source technologies without requiring specialized hardware for the current prototype. Its responsive interface is designed for desktop and smaller screens.

Beyond space exploration, the underlying local-first concept may also offer opportunities for digital health-support applications in remote environments and other settings with limited connectivity.

9. LIMITATIONS, SAFETY AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

COSMOCURA is an educational software prototype, not a clinically validated medical device. It has not been operationally tested in spaceflight. Health measurements are manually entered, and the system does not currently connect to spacecraft sensors, NASA systems, radiation-monitoring instruments or mission control.

The local SQLite database is not encrypted, and the backend service must remain running for the application to operate. Emergency information is not a substitute for professional medical assessment or mission-approved medical procedures.

Future development could explore encrypted health records, expert-reviewed medical guidance, validated sensor integration, NASA and space-agency data integration, mission-approved emergency workflows and more advanced offline capabilities.

AI ASSISTANCE DISCLOSURE

ChatGPT was used as an assistive tool during brainstorming, research, software architecture planning, code generation, debugging, documentation, and presentation preparation. AI-generated visual assets were used where applicable and are identified accordingly.

The submitted COSMOCURA prototype does not currently contain an integrated runtime AI or machine-learning model. Its demonstrated functions operate through programmed application logic and locally stored data. The team directed the project, made implementation decisions, and reviewed and tested the application with AI assistance.

OUR VISION

We believe that access to organized health information should not become a limitation when humanity travels beyond Earth.

COSMOCURA is our contribution towards exploring a future where technology helps make healthcare information more accessible, understandable and actionable — wherever the mission takes us.
